title: Reverse Linked List
source: canonical Reverse Linked List concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is the first node of a singly linked list; each node holds an integer and points to the next node. Reverse the direction of the links so the last node becomes the first, and return the first node of the reversed list. The ListNode class is provided in the starter code.

examples.explanation: Every link flips: 5 points to 4, 4 points to 3, and so on.

hints: Walk the list once, keeping a pointer to the piece you have already reversed.
Three pointers are enough: the node in hand, the node before it, and the node after it.
Save head.next, point head.next at previous, then slide previous and head one step forward. Return previous at the end.
solution: Three-pointer sweep: for every node, redirect its next pointer at the previously seen node and advance. Each node is touched once: O(n) time, O(1) space.
solutionCode:
def reverse_list(head):
    previous = None
    while head is not None:
        following = head.next
        head.next = previous
        previous = head
        head = following
    return previous
